name: DesignThink: Human-Centered Innovation
description: Simulation where learners apply the five-stage Design Thinking process (Empathize, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test) to solve a healthcare appointment adherence crisis at Meridia Health Systems. Teams manage a constrained innovation budget, allocate research time, and navigate organizational politics while discovering that the root cause is behavioral, not technological.

howtoplay:
# How to Play — DesignThink: Human-Centered Innovation

You are the innovation team at Meridia Health Systems, a 12-clinic network in Bogotá, Lima and Santiago with a 34% appointment no-show crisis. Two digital fixes have already failed. You have **$240,000** and **120 team-hours** across **4 rounds** — spend them wisely; every round must stay affordable.

**Round 1 — Empathize.** Allocate research hours (interviews $2,000/hr, observation $1,500/hr, desk review $800/hr) and pick a patient segment to focus on. Different methods surface different truths — what patients *say* is not always what they *need*. Your Insight Depth stays hidden until your prototype meets users.

**Round 2 — Define.** Choose the "How Might We" statement your research supports, invest convergence hours ($1,000/hr) to sharpen it, and decide how to update your stakeholders. A sharp framing of the *wrong* problem is still the wrong problem.

**Round 3 — Ideate & Prototype.** Pick an ideation approach, a prototype type (storyboard to digital wireframe) and extra budget. Match fidelity to how validated your problem definition is — polish before validation is waste. Manage your sponsor's expectations; if the CEO demands a digital pivot, choose your response carefully.

**Round 4 — Test.** Choose a test method and participant count (5–50, $200 each), then persist, pivot, or redefine based on the evidence.

**Scoring (0–100):** Insight Depth 30% · Prototype-Problem Fit 35% · Stakeholder Alignment 20% · Process Discipline 15%, modulated by your test's Learning Yield. Penalties: Speed Trap −15, Analysis Paralysis −10, Wrong Problem −20. 70+ is Excellent. Watch for surprise events — they roll once and they stick.
teachingnote:
# Teaching Note — Sim 134 "DesignThink: Human-Centered Innovation"

**Level:** MBA / ExecEd / corporate innovation · **Session:** 90 min (4 rounds × ~15 min + debrief) · **Teams:** 3–6 of 3–4 · **Full TN:** STR-2026-134_TN.md · **Case:** STR-2026-134

**Setup (15 min).** Brief the Meridia scenario (34% no-show, $240K, two failed digital fixes). **Do not lecture Design Thinking first** — the framework emerges through play.

**Hidden root cause:** patients decline to *book* follow-ups because they cannot predict transport + childcare availability. Logistics and social capital, not communication. Only observation-weighted research surfaces it; interviews return "I forgot" (true but not causal).

**Facilitator mechanics (v1.1.0):** the Insight Depth meter shows "—" until the prototype is built — if teams ask, say "you'll know when your prototype meets users." The CEO digital-pivot response selector appears in Round 3 only for teams whose Round-2 event fired. Validation prevents any team from spending itself into a dead end. Events roll once and persist through undo.

**Between-round prompts:** R1: "What surprised you? What do you still not know?" · R2: "Read your HMW to another team — can they tell what problem it describes?" · R3: "If your prototype shipped at full scale today, what % of no-shows would it cut — and how do you know?"

**Watch for:** desk-review-heavy allocations (interviewing administrators, not patients); teams that guess the right HMW without research (clarity gates on insight — the model calls the bluff); over-research (>85 hrs by R3 = Analysis Paralysis −10); the default 15 test participants (halves the sample factor of Learning Yield).

**Score anatomy:** Insight 30 / Fit 35 / Alignment 20 / Discipline 15, × Learning Yield modifier (0.70–1.00); penalties −15/−10/−20. Benchmarks: disciplined play ≈ 85–94 · defaults ≈ 42 · rush + reminder-app HMW < 20 · deep research but CEO-compliant digital pivot ≈ mid-40s.

**Debrief (15 min):** (1) said vs. needed — which method exposed the gap? (2) which HMWs reframed vs. restated? (3) when does fidelity stop buying learning? (4) push back, compromise, or comply — and what made push-back affordable? (5) persist/pivot/redefine — evidence or sunk cost? Close on: a failed prototype that redefines the problem is cheaper than launching the wrong solution.
casestudy:
# DesignThink: Meridia Health Systems — Cracking a 34% No-Show Rate (STR-2026-134)

**Setting:** Bogotá · Lima · Santiago, June 2026. Meridia Health Systems, a private 12-clinic urban primary-care network (USD 36M revenue, 380,000 annual visits), runs a **34% appointment no-show rate** against an 18% regional benchmark. A 2024 SMS reminder app and a 2025 scheduling-software replacement burned **USD 330K** combined and moved the rate 0.9 points. The CFO prices the annual leakage at **USD 4.1M**.

**The protagonist.** Valentina Reyes, 39, Directora de Experiencia del Paciente e Innovación, must commit a four-round Design-Thinking cycle on a **USD 240K envelope and 120 team-hours**: Empathize (research-hour allocation across interviews, waiting-room observation and desk review; segment focus), Define ("How Might We" framing, convergence, stakeholder update), Ideate-and-Prototype (approach, fidelity, sponsor expectations), Test (method, participants, persist/pivot/redefine). The CEO has promised the board a scalable solution in six months — and may demand a mid-cycle pivot back to a digital app. A quarterly cost review may cut the remaining envelope by 25%.

**What the interviews said:** "se me olvidó" — I forgot (44%) · work conflict (27%) · transport (16%) · childcare (9%).
**What observation showed:** patients at the front desk **declining to book follow-ups at all** — because they cannot predict, weeks out, whether transport and childcare will both hold on the day. A booking-confidence problem: logistics and social capital, not memory.

**The options.** (A) Observation-weighted research / barrier-reduction HMW / matched-fidelity physical service mock-up / interview-tested — modelled Innovation Score ≈ 90. (B) Rush-to-ideate / reminder-app HMW / USD 35K digital wireframe — Speed Trap and Wrong Problem penalties, score < 20: the two prior failures, reproduced at speed. (C) Deep research / right framing / CEO-compliant digital pivot — score mid-40s: good research overridden in the room where the prototype was chosen.

**Decision:** Which envelope — and if the CEO calls demanding the app, do you push back with evidence (USD 8K), compromise on a parallel pilot (USD 4K), or comply?

*Full case: STR-2026-134 (~2,000 words, with exhibits). Companion teaching note: STR-2026-134_TN.md. Disguised; frameworks are real.*
